question: Does resolving a whole-screen visual target before functional routes improve the first delivery?
status: submitted; independent reviewer passed, parent visual assessment below requested quality

scopeChecks.professionalMail: Quiet familiar surfaces remain appropriate; separate visual exploration not required.
scopeChecks.textLedGame: Styled native shapes and typography can resolve the whole visual target; generated art is not required.
scopeChecks.smallEstablishedEdit: Existing suitable screen supplies the visual target; no redesign process.
scopeChecks.passiveHUD: No invented choices or actions; plan only the states the requested task uses.

validation.full: 41 selected producers passed. NARROWED: reference-host benchmark and recorded native-Studio host deferred; three special tiers unselected. Separate benchmark PASS; package build/status complete. Exact 14-file hashes match the frozen candidate.

limits: One unseen task cannot establish a general success rate.
A visual study is not a delivered runtime UI.
A first delivery may include internal drafts, critique and repairs.
progress: Created native planet artwork and a styled prototype, with design notes.
Initial device checks found short-landscape clipping and small Xbox text; builder repaired these before first independent review.
Pointer and keyboard routes pass according to builder, including focus transfer.
Actual emulator captures cover desktop, iPhone 17 Pro portrait/landscape, and Xbox.
First independent review marked all eight views revise: parcel-delivery character and payoff are too dependent on text. Builder is repairing and recapturing with no parent visual feedback.
operationalAssistance: Copied the existing pinned rokit.toml to resolve tools in the isolated kit.
Held secondary Studio until the earlier submission was frozen, then released it.
Offered a parent native-controller check on unchanged frozen source after submission.
reviewOutcome: Three independent rounds. First two rejected all submitted views on identity. Third passed all ten final views at 4/4/5/4/4. Parent disagrees that this establishes the requested visual finish.

parentAssessment.visual: Clearer and more specific than the first draft, with a tiny alien, parcel and destination and an illustrated state change. Still a large generic button bank beside/under simple artwork; sparse composition and ordinary control surfaces do not reach the requested level. Reviewer pass is retained but not adopted as proof.
parentAssessment.referenceLimit: Only the kit rank-card design exercise was inspected as an image. Public game-reference pixels were unavailable to the builder. This is weaker than the task-relevant shipped-game comparison required by the guidance.
parentAssessment.studyLimit: DESIGN.md describes a native implementation as the styled study pending Studio captures; there is no separate inspected whole-screen mockup before functional implementation.
parentAssessment.controls: Facet selection/action buttons and native drawings, with explicit focus transfer. Parent native gamepad route passed, including automatic focus after dispatch/return and no hold-A cascade.
parentAssessment.copy: The pre-dispatch Mars helper says A oversized hat; a minor copy defect remains in the frozen source.
parentAssessment.devices: Actual desktop/iPhone 17 Pro portrait and landscape/Xbox simulator captures. Parent native Xbox controller check on frozen source; hardware touch not claimed.
parentAssessment.qualityConclusion: This supports functional and responsive progress, not a broad claim that first deliveries reach the requested game-art quality.
